doc.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: The waiter job and the dropped tray
summary: His only non-music job was waiting tables, ended by dropping his first tray.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Have you ever had to work a non-music job in your career?
Oh you mean since I’ve become a musician?
No. No after I became a musician I didn’t have to go outside to work anything. But before, before I became a professional musician I had a job as a waiter, and I dropped my first tray.
My first tray. So the guy said, “Don’t worry about it,” he said, “everybody drops their first tray.” That was my last tray too.
I think it was prophetic. Well it was good for the music business that you dropped your first tray.
Filled with dishes you know, in this big hotel, luxury restaurant.
